metaDescription: Himalayan vaccine schedule with core ages in weeks. Set reminders so Himalayan boosters are not missed.

bodySections.heading: Why timing matters for this schedule
paragraphs: The Himalayan core series (FVRCP plus rabies per law) is plotted at 8, 12, 16, 16 weeks in the table above so a medium kitten is covered as maternal antibodies fade.
At 7-14 lb (3-6.5 kg), Himalayan visit logistics matter as much as antigens: book the 16-week appointment before class, daycare, or boarding asks for proof.
Bring polycystic kidney disease (pkd) risk and brachycephalic concerns into the Himalayan exam-room conversation while you are already there for shots.
Rabies for a Himalayan still follows local statute, and when the clinic allows you can pair it with the ≥16-week core finish, then photograph the certificate into PetClues the same day.

bodySections.heading: If a dose is missed or delayed
paragraphs: If your Himalayan misses the dose scheduled near week 12, call the clinic the same day with product names — do not restart the Himalayan series from memory.
The danger for a delayed Himalayan is the gap, not the embarrassment, because panleukopenia pressure stays real for an under-vaccinated kitten even in clean-looking neighborhoods.
While waiting for the make-up FVRCP visit, skip high-traffic dog parks / unknown-cat intros and keep the Himalayan away from unvaccinated animals.
After catch-up, rewrite reminders for the next Himalayan due date (7, 3, and 1 day prior) so the same miss does not recur.

faqs.question: When does the Himalayan core vaccine series usually finish?
faqs.answer: This breed record completes core vaccines around 16 weeks of age, with rabies timed per local law. Your clinic may adjust intervals for the individual kitten.

faqs.question: What should I do if my Himalayan misses a booster?
faqs.answer: Contact your veterinarian for a catch-up plan instead of restarting or skipping ahead. Keep prior dates handy and limit high-risk exposure until the series is current again.

faqs.question: Where can I read Himalayan health context beyond vaccines?
faqs.answer: See the Himalayan adult health guide for breed predispositions such as polycystic kidney disease (pkd) risk, then bring those notes to wellness and vaccine visits.
